findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Compromise of this user's credentials permits complete control of compute, storage, serverless and monitoring across the account, including data exfiltration from any S3 bucket and privilege escalation via lambda/ec2 role passing patterns.

A permanent IAM access key is created for the user with no PGP key specified, so the plaintext secret is stored unencrypted in Terraform state. Long-lived static keys attached to a wildcard-permission user are a high-value target and cannot be rotated automatically.
Because no pgp_key is set, the secret access key is persisted in cleartext in the Terraform state file, exposing credentials to anyone with read access to the state backend.

An IAM user is provisioned with directly attached inline permissions and static access keys instead of a role assumed via federation or an instance/service principal, creating unmanaged, non-expiring credentials outside centralised identity control.
